text:
**No, the next ship date hasn't changed.** S-104's next open order is still PO005791: 4,200 units of RM-221 (Polysorbate 80), promised to ship **2026-10-07**, and it hasn't shipped yet.

**What we concluded last time** (the saved answer on customer exposure to S-104)
- S-104 is Delmar Specialty Chemicals, a tier-2 supplier in India. Its next ship date puts the **Lacrivia and cyclosporine dry-eye products at risk**:
  - Lacrivia 0.1% 5 mL: 7,017 TRx over 13 weeks
  - Lacrivia 0.1% 10 mL: 3,425 TRx
  - Cyclosporine 0.05% 5 mL: 3,544 TRx
  - Lens care solutions FG-3001 to 3011 are also fed by RM-221, but they aren't in the commercial data.
- In total that's 13,986 TRx across 35 top-level customers. Eight health systems carry 77% of it. Oak Hollow, Riverbend and Northfield have Tier A supply contracts.
- RM-221 has only one qualified supplier, S-104. It takes about 50 days from S-104 shipping until Lacrivia 5 mL reaches the DC, including the 14-day sterility test, so the earliest DC arrival is about 2026-11-26. Any slip moves that back day for day.
- Cyclosporine shouldn't be offered as a Lacrivia substitute, because the same RM-221 supply feeds it (BR-SUB-01).
- Oculon (FG-2001/2002) wasn't exposed. It uses S-104's other material, RM-222 (benzalkonium chloride), which has a qualified backup supplier, S-130.

**Changes since then: none of significance**

| Item | Last time | Now (data as of 2026-09-30) |
|---|---|---|
| Next RM-221 order (PO005791) | Promised 2026-10-07, open | Promised 2026-10-07, open, 4,200 units |
| Next RM-222 order (PO000430) | Due 2026-10-26 | Promised 2026-10-26, open, 2,600 units |
| Qualified suppliers for RM-221 | S-104 only (S-131 not qualified) | Same: still the only supplier |
| Qualified suppliers for RM-222 | S-104 plus S-130 | Same |

There's also a later open RM-221 order, PO000369 (3,300 units, promised 2026-10-29). The earlier answer didn't mention it, so I can't tell whether it's new. Both PO000369 and PO000430 have an order date of 2026-10-02, after the data's as-of date, so they may be planned orders entered ahead of time.

**Risk on PO005791:** S-104 has shipped RM-221 late on **25% of 48 closed orders**, averaging about **12 days late** when it slips. Two of its last five RM-221 orders were late: PO000360 by 14 days and PO000363 by 8 days. A typical 12-day slip would push DC recovery for Lacrivia 5 mL from about 2026-11-26 to about 2026-12-08. That date is my estimate using the 50-day lead time from last time; I didn't rerun the lead-time tool. RM-222 ships late more often (40%, about 13 days), but it has a backup supplier.

**Sources and definitions**
- The saved past answer from the knowledge layer, on customer exposure to S-104.
- Supply data: `dbo.PURCH_ORD` (open orders and on-time history), `dbo.SUPPLIER`, `dbo.MATERIAL`, `dbo.SUPPLIER_MATERIAL`.
- Late-ship rate is the ratified Supply Planning definition: closed orders shipped after the promised date, divided by all closed orders. I didn't use the deprecated archive table `PURCH_ORD_ARCHIVE`.
- Supplier counts use the ratified qualified-supplier count (1 means a single source).
- Rules applied: BR-LEAD-01 (recovery lead time) and BR-SUB-01 (approved substitutes).
- I didn't rerun the products-affected walk or the customer TRx ranking. Neither the bill-of-materials path nor the ship date has changed, so the last answer's exposure numbers still apply.

question: What did we conclude last time about exposure to supplier S-104, and has its next ship date changed since?
answer:
**No, the next ship date hasn't changed.** S-104's next open order is still PO005791: 4,200 units of RM-221 (Polysorbate 80), promised to ship **2026-10-07**, and it hasn't shipped yet.

**What we concluded last time** (the saved answer on customer exposure to S-104)
- S-104 is Delmar Specialty Chemicals, a tier-2 supplier in India. Its next ship date puts the **Lacrivia and cyclosporine dry-eye products at risk**:
  - Lacrivia 0.1% 5 mL: 7,017 TRx over 13 weeks
  - Lacrivia 0.1% 10 mL: 3,425 TRx
  - Cyclosporine 0.05% 5 mL: 3,544 TRx
  - Lens care solutions FG-3001 to 3011 are also fed by RM-221, but they aren't in the commercial data.
- In total that's 13,986 TRx across 35 top-level customers. Eight health systems carry 77% of it. Oak Hollow, Riverbend and Northfield have Tier A supply contracts.
- RM-221 has only one qualified supplier, S-104. It takes about 50 days from S-104 shipping until Lacrivia 5 mL reaches the DC, including the 14-day sterility test, so the earliest DC arrival is about 2026-11-26. Any slip moves that back day for day.
- Cyclosporine shouldn't be offered as a Lacrivia substitute, because the same RM-221 supply feeds it (BR-SUB-01).
- Oculon (FG-2001/2002) wasn't exposed. It uses S-104's other material, RM-222 (benzalkonium chloride), which has a qualified backup supplier, S-130.

**Changes since then: none of significance**

| Item | Last time | Now (data as of 2026-09-30) |
|---|---|---|
| Next RM-221 order (PO005791) | Promised 2026-10-07, open | Promised 2026-10-07, open, 4,200 units |
| Next RM-222 order (PO000430) | Due 2026-10-26 | Promised 2026-10-26, open, 2,600 units |
| Qualified suppliers for RM-221 | S-104 only (S-131 not qualified) | Same: still the only supplier |
| Qualified suppliers for RM-222 | S-104 plus S-130 | Same |

There's also a later open RM-221 order, PO000369 (3,300 units, promised 2026-10-29). The earlier answer didn't mention it, so I can't tell whether it's new. Both PO000369 and PO000430 have an order date of 2026-10-02, after the data's as-of date, so they may be planned orders entered ahead of time.

**Risk on PO005791:** S-104 has shipped RM-221 late on **25% of 48 closed orders**, averaging about **12 days late** when it slips. Two of its last five RM-221 orders were late: PO000360 by 14 days and PO000363 by 8 days. A typical 12-day slip would push DC recovery for Lacrivia 5 mL from about 2026-11-26 to about 2026-12-08. That date is my estimate using the 50-day lead time from last time; I didn't rerun the lead-time tool. RM-222 ships late more often (40%, about 13 days), but it has a backup supplier.

**Sources and definitions**
- The saved past answer from the knowledge layer, on customer exposure to S-104.
- Supply data: `dbo.PURCH_ORD` (open orders and on-time history), `dbo.SUPPLIER`, `dbo.MATERIAL`, `dbo.SUPPLIER_MATERIAL`.
- Late-ship rate is the ratified Supply Planning definition: closed orders shipped after the promised date, divided by all closed orders. I didn't use the deprecated archive table `PURCH_ORD_ARCHIVE`.
- Supplier counts use the ratified qualified-supplier count (1 means a single source).
- Rules applied: BR-LEAD-01 (recovery lead time) and BR-SUB-01 (approved substitutes).
- I didn't rerun the products-affected walk or the customer TRx ranking. Neither the bill-of-materials path nor the ship date has changed, so the last answer's exposure numbers still apply.
